Sorting and recycling

Demolition waste removal and recycling, sorted on the way out

Removal of demolition waste with the recoverable material separated rather than tipped whole. Concrete and brick to crushing, steel to scrap recovery, sound timber recovered where it can be, and only what is genuinely mixed going to a waste facility to be sorted there. Tell us what is coming out of the building, and we will quote the removal and the recycling.

The detail

Why separating on site usually pays for itself

  • Mixed waste is charged as mixed waste. One load of unsorted material is charged at the highest applicable rate for everything in it.
  • Clean concrete has a cheaper destination. Crushing and recycling, rather than landfill, and the difference in gate rate is substantial.
  • Steel has value rather than cost. Separated steel goes to scrap recovery. On a commercial or industrial job it is often the most valuable thing leaving the site.
  • Sorting costs machine time. Which is real, and on most jobs still less than the disposal saving it produces.
  • It needs to be planned. Separation happens as the structure comes down. Doing it after is picking through a pile, which costs far more.
  • Asbestos has to be out first. Mixed into demolition waste it contaminates the whole stream and the whole stream is then charged and handled as asbestos.

Before you book

What people ask about this one

What actually gets recycled?
Clean concrete and brick are crushed and recycled, commonly as road base. Steel and other metals go to scrap recovery. Sound timber is recovered where it can be. What is genuinely mixed goes to a licensed waste facility to be sorted there.
Does separating cost more?
It costs machine time and saves disposal cost, and on most jobs the saving is the larger of the two. On a job with a lot of clean concrete or structural steel it is not close.
Can you sort material that is already in a pile?
It can be done but it is expensive, because picking through mixed material is far slower than separating it as it falls. Planning the separation before demolition starts is what makes it worth doing.
What if there is asbestos in the waste?
There should not be, because it is removed under clearance before demolition. If it is found in the stream, the stream stops and is handled under the asbestos pathway.
Do I get proof of where it went?
Dockets from each facility, handed to you. On a job with a recycling target in the approval, those are what demonstrate it was met.

Construction type and approximate size. What a building is made of decides how much of it can be recovered, and that is what decides the disposal cost.
